title: Rollout Orchestrator: create/progress/pause/rollback APIs + lifecycle state machine
author: Hannah Rivera
description:
Context: This PR introduces the first GA-shaped version of the Rollout Orchestrator service for Hosted canary rollouts. It adds the external (Console backend-facing) APIs for creating rollouts and driving the lifecycle (start, advance step, pause/resume, rollback), plus the core rollout state machine and persistence layer interactions. The goal is to make rollout execution deterministic, auditable, and safe to operate (idempotency, transition validation, and clear error messages), while keeping stop-conditions/auto-rollback wiring to follow in a dedicated PR.

What’s included: 1) Rollout lifecycle state machine: - States: DRAFT -> READY -> RUNNING -> PAUSED -> COMPLETED; terminal rollback path: RUNNING/PAUSED -> ROLLING_BACK -> ROLLED_BACK. - Failure state: FAILED (only for internal errors; customer-initiated rollback uses ROLLING_BACK/ROLLED_BACK). - Transition rules enforced centrally (cannot advance step when PAUSED, cannot pause when DRAFT, cannot rollback after COMPLETED, etc). - Optimistic concurrency via rollout.version with compare-and-swap updates to prevent concurrent step changes.

2) Orchestrator APIs (internal HTTP+JSON used by Console backend): - POST /v1/rollouts: create a rollout in DRAFT with baseline + canary targets and optional step plan. - POST /v1/rollouts/{id}:start: validates plan + sets READY/RUNNING depending on whether first step is 0% or >0%. - POST /v1/rollouts/{id}:advance: moves to the next configured traffic step (or accepts an explicit target_percent when allow_manual_step=true). - POST /v1/rollouts/{id}:pause and :resume: controls execution without modifying the saved plan. - POST /v1/rollouts/{id}:rollback: sets traffic to baseline and moves into ROLLING_BACK, then marks ROLLED_BACK once routing confirmation is recorded.

3) Initial validations and guardrails (policy engine hooks come in ENG-9146 / PR-28802): - Traffic steps must be monotonically increasing and between 0..100 inclusive. - Total canary percent is interpreted as “percent of eligible traffic on the route” (does not bypass existing routing policies). - Baseline and canary targets must refer to the same logical route and compatible model family (schema-level check; deeper compatibility checks are deferred). - Minimum soak time is validated if provided (>= 60s), but enforcement of soak timers for auto-advance is NOT included here (Console triggers step changes explicitly for now).

4) Event emission (foundational, not full audit logging): - Emits rollout.lifecycle events on create/start/advance/pause/resume/rollback to the internal event bus (rollout_events topic). - Payload includes: rollout_id, route_id, actor (if provided), previous_state, new_state, previous_step, new_step, requested_canary_percent, effective_canary_percent, request_id. - Note: customer-visible Audit Log events will be added in PR-28877; this PR focuses on consistent lifecycle events for telemetry + future audit mapping.

5) Tests: - Unit tests for transition guards and idempotent requests. - Integration tests for DB persistence + version CAS behavior (simulated concurrent advance calls).

Out of scope / follow-ups: - Auto-stop/rollback on SLO breach (ENG-9158 / PR-28845). - Policy engine enforcement for approvers/max step/soak (ENG-9146 / PR-28802). - Customer-facing timeline rendering (Console UI).

Operational notes: - All mutating endpoints accept Idempotency-Key; server stores (rollout_id, endpoint, idempotency_key) -> response for 24h to ensure Console retries are safe. - Error responses are normalized into {code, message, details} for Console to display guardrail errors vs transient errors.

Release/rollout: feature-flagged by tenant in Console backend; orchestrator endpoints are dark until the flag is enabled. No migrations are required beyond the rollout table added in ENG-9131 (already merged).
commits: rollout-orchestrator: add rollout service skeleton + routing adapter interface
state-machine: define lifecycle states/transitions + transition validator
persistence: CAS updates + idempotency key storage
events: emit rollout.lifecycle events for mutating actions
tests: transition unit tests + concurrent advance integration test
docs: add minimal API README + error code mapping
conversation:
Jada Williams (review): The transition rules look mostly good, but I’m worried about idempotency on :advance. If Console retries after a 504, we could advance twice. Can we store the idempotency key per (rollout_id, action) and return the previous response? Also please add a test for “double advance” with same key. Hannah Rivera (author): Good call. Added idempotency table + repository and wired it into all mutating endpoints. Added tests for retrying :advance and :rollback with the same Idempotency-Key.

Chloe Martin (review): API surface is close, but can we normalize error codes? Console needs to distinguish “invalid transition” vs “policy denies” vs “transient dependency.” I’d prefer explicit codes like ROLLOUT_INVALID_STATE and ROLLOUT_VALIDATION_FAILED. Hannah Rivera (author): Updated error mapper. Transition violations return ROLLOUT_INVALID_STATE (409). Validation failures return ROLLOUT_VALIDATION_FAILED (400). Downstream routing adapter failures return ROLLOUT_DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE (503) with retry-after.

Ethan Park (review): Two concerns: (1) optimistic concurrency should fail with a clear message if version mismatches; (2) rollback should explicitly set desired_canary_percent=0 and persist that before calling the router to avoid split-brain after a crash. Also please add a note on recovery semantics. Hannah Rivera (author): Addressed both. CAS mismatch returns 409 with a “rollout_modified” detail so Console can refetch. Rollback now persists desired_canary_percent=0 and state=ROLLING_BACK first, then calls router. README updated with crash recovery notes: on startup we reconcile ROLLING_BACK rollouts by checking router desired state and finalizing.

Sean Gallagher (review): From an SRE perspective: can we emit metrics counters for transitions and failures, and make sure events include request_id and actor when available? Also: please don’t emit FAILED on user errors; FAILED should be for internal failures only. Hannah Rivera (author): Added metrics: rollout_action_total{action,result}, rollout_transition_total{from,to}, rollout_dependency_error_total{dependency}. Events now include request_id and actor fields. Adjusted FAILED usage to internal only; user errors return 4xx without changing state.

Final review: Jada approved after idempotency + tests landed. Chloe approved after error code normalization. Ethan approved after rollback ordering fix. Sean approved after metrics/event fields.

release_notes: Internal: Rollout Orchestrator now supports the core lifecycle APIs required by the Hosted canary rollout workflow (create/start/advance/pause/resume/rollback) with idempotent mutations, validated state transitions, and lifecycle event emission for telemetry/audit follow-ups.
